title: Constant degree of a finite etale cover of a connected scheme, and trace after restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme] and $f:Y\to X$ a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then there is an integer $d\ge0$ such that (a) $f$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; (b) for every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the geometric fibre $Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has exactly $d$ points (it is $\coprod_{i=1}^d\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$); (c) for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], with the restriction and trace of [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace],\n$$F\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}_{f,F}}f_*f^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}}F$$\nis multiplication by $d$.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), after Definition 03SE: 'This description shows that if $f$ has constant degree $d$, then the composition $\mathcal F\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is multiplication by $d$'; local splitting: Etale Morphisms Lemma 04HN

proof.text: *$f$ is finite locally free.* By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $f$ is finite, and etale means locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism]. So $f$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, which is the definition of a finite locally free morphism [def-pc-finite-locally-free] (Stacks Lemma 02KB: equivalently, $f$ is affine and $f_*\mathcal O_Y$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module).

*Constant degree: assertion (a).* For $x\in X$ let $\delta_f(x)=\dim_{\kappa(x)}\Gamma(Y_x,\mathcal O_{Y_x})$, $Y_x=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant], $\delta_f$ is a locally constant function $X\to\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$. $X$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], in particular nonempty; pick $x_0\in X$ and put $d=\delta_f(x_0)\ge0$. The set $T_1=\delta_f^{-1}(d)$ is open (every point of it has an open neighbourhood on which $\delta_f$ is constant, equal to $d$), and so is $T_2=X\setminus T_1=\bigcup_{e\ne d}\delta_f^{-1}(e)$; thus $X=T_1\amalg T_2$ with $T_1,T_2$ open and closed, and $x_0\in T_1$, so $T_2=\varnothing$ by connectedness. Hence $\delta_f(x)=d$ for all $x\in X$, i.e. $f$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. This is (a).

source.place: Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 04MH (lemma-finite-locally-free) and the remark after Definition 02KA ('S is the disjoint union of open and closed subschemes S_d ...'); the connectedness argument is the one-line consequence for connected S

proof.text: *The geometric fibre has degree $d$.* Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] lying over $x\in X$; it is the composite of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ (from a field map $\kappa(x)\to\Omega$) and the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ containing $x$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; since $f$ is finite, $f^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finite $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $\bar x$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ factor through $V$ via $R\to\kappa(x)\to\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (the preimage of $V$ in $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, resp. $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, is everything) and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=f^{-1}(V)\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\Omega)$ and $Y_x=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(x))$. Since $A\otimes_R\Omega=(A\otimes_R\kappa(x))\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\Omega$ and a $\kappa(x)$-basis of $A\otimes_R\kappa(x)$ maps to an $\Omega$-basis of its base change, $\dim_\Omega\Gamma(Y_{\bar x},\mathcal O)=\dim_{\kappa(x)}\Gamma(Y_x,\mathcal O)=d$ by step 2, where $Y_{\bar x}=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$.

source.place: Stacks Morphisms, Definition 02KA and Lemma 02KD (lemma-base-change-finite-locally-free); written out by the agent

proof.text: *Assertion (b).* $f$ is finite etale, so $Y$ is an object of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(X)$ [def-galois-categories], and $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, hence separably closed. By [lem-galois-geometric-fibre] the geometric fibre $Y_{\bar x}$ is, over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, a finite disjoint union $\coprod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for some $n\ge0$. Then $\Gamma(Y_{\bar x},\mathcal O)\cong\Omega^n$ as $\Omega$-algebras, of $\Omega$-dimension $n$, so $n=d$ by step 3; and $\coprod_{i=1}^d\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has exactly $d$ points. This is (b).

source.place: Stacks Morphisms Lemma 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field) / Algebra Lemma 00U3 (an etale algebra over a separably closed field is a finite product of copies of it), as packaged in lem-galois-geometric-fibre; the count is step 3

proof.text: *Etale local splitting with $d$ copies.* Let $x\in X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] there are an etale $g_x:U_x\to X$, a point $u_x\in U_x$ over $x$, a finite set $J_x$ and a decomposition $Y\times_XU_x=\coprod_{j\in J_x}V_j$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes such that each $V_j\to U_x$ (restriction of the projection $f_x:Y\times_XU_x\to U_x$) is an isomorphism. We show $\#J_x=d$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(u_x)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_x$ be the geometric point over $u_x$ [def-weil-geometric-point]; then $\bar x=g_x\circ\bar u$ is a geometric point of $X$ over $x$. By the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] (pasting of two cartesian squares), $Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\cong(Y\times_XU_x)\times_{U_x}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] the latter is the disjoint union of the open and closed subschemes $V_j\times_{U_x}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $j\in J_x$, each isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ because $V_j\to U_x$ is an isomorphism. So the geometric fibre at $\bar x$ has $\#J_x$ points, and by (b) (step 4) $\#J_x=d$. Number $J_x=\{1,\dots,d\}$ and let $\sigma_i:U_x\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i$ be the inverse of $V_i\to U_x$. Then $Y\times_XU_x$ together with the open immersions $\sigma_i$ (which cover it, with pairwise empty intersections) is a coproduct $\coprod_{i=1}^dU_x$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-copies] (a morphism out of a scheme covered by disjoint open subschemes is the same as a family of morphisms out of the pieces, by gluing of morphisms), and $f_x$ is the codiagonal: $f_x\circ\sigma_i=\mathrm{id}_{U_x}$ for every $i$.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04HN (lemma-finite-etale-etale-local), used as in Etale Cohomology Section 03SH after Definition 03SE ('every finite etale morphism is etale locally on X of the form given in (2) for some integer d'); the count d is written out by the agent

proof.text: *Restriction and trace commute with the localization $g_x$.* Fix $x$, write $g=g_x$, $U=U_x$, $Y'=Y\times_XU$, $f'=f_x:Y'\to U$ (a base change of $f$, so finite etale) and $G=g^{-1}F\in\Ab(U_{\Et})$. For an object $W$ of $U_{\Et}$ (viewed in $X_{\Et}$ through $g$) one has $W\times_UY'=W\times_XY$ with the same projection to $W$ (pasting, [def-pc-fibre-product]). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], applied to the etale morphisms $g$, $f$ and $f'$, up to the natural isomorphisms $\rho$ there: $G(W)=F(W)$; $(f^{-1}F)(V)=F(V)$ and $(f'^{-1}G)(V)=F(V)$ for $V$ etale over $Y$, resp. $Y'$; the unit $\operatorname{res}_{f,F}=\eta_f(F)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace] at $W$ is the restriction $F(W)\to F(W\times_XY)$ along the projection, and $\operatorname{res}_{f',G}$ at $W$ is the restriction $G(W)=F(W)\to F(W\times_UY')=F(W\times_XY)$ along the same projection. So $g^{-1}\operatorname{res}_{f,F}=\operatorname{res}_{f',G}$ under the canonical identification $g^{-1}f_*f^{-1}F=f'_*f'^{-1}G$ of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists](1) (on $W$ both sides are $F(W\times_XY)$), and by property (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists], $g^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}=\operatorname{tr}_{f',G}$ under the same identification. As $g^{-1}$ is additive, $g^{-1}(\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}\circ\operatorname{res}_{f,F}-d\cdot\mathrm{id}_F)=\operatorname{tr}_{f',G}\circ\operatorname{res}_{f',G}-d\cdot\mathrm{id}_G$.

source.place: Stacks Etale Cohomology Section 03SH after Definition 03SE, property (1) of the characterization ('it commutes with etale localization on X'); the compatibility of res is written out by the agent

proof.text: *The split case: $\operatorname{tr}\circ\operatorname{res}=d$.* With the notation of step 6 and $Y'=\coprod_{i=1}^dV_i$, $\sigma_i:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i$ (step 5), let $W$ be an object of $U_{\Et}$. Then $W\times_UY'$ is the disjoint union of the open and closed subschemes $W_i=W\times_UV_i$, each mapped isomorphically onto $W$ by the projection $p_i$ (base change of the isomorphism $V_i\to U$), and these form a covering of $W\times_UY'$ in $U_{\Et}$ with empty pairwise fibre products [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-copies]. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] (with $G(\varnothing)=0$, the empty covering) gives $G(W\times_UY')\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^dG(W_i)$, $t\mapsto(t|_{W_i})_i$, and composing with $(p_i^*)^{-1}:G(W_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(W)$ gives the identification $(f'_*f'^{-1}G)(W)=G(W)^{d}$ of property (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists]; by that property ($Y'$ is the disjoint union of $d$ open and closed subschemes each mapped isomorphically onto $U$ by $f'$, i.e. $Y'=\coprod_{i=1}^dU$ with $f'$ the identity on each summand, via the $\sigma_i$), $\operatorname{tr}_{f',G}(W)$ is the sum map $G(W)^d\to G(W)$. By step 6, $\operatorname{res}_{f',G}(W)(s)=s|_{W\times_UY'}$ for $s\in G(W)$; its $i$-th component is $(p_i^*)^{-1}(s|_{W_i})=(p_i^*)^{-1}(p_i^*s)=s$, since the composite $W_i\hookrightarrow W\times_UY'\to W$ is $p_i$. So $\operatorname{res}_{f',G}(W)$ is the diagonal $s\mapsto(s,\dots,s)$, and $\operatorname{tr}_{f',G}(\operatorname{res}_{f',G}(s))=s+\dots+s=d\cdot s$. Hence $\operatorname{tr}_{f',G}\circ\operatorname{res}_{f',G}=d\cdot\mathrm{id}_G$, and by step 6, $g_x^{-1}(\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}\circ\operatorname{res}_{f,F}-d\cdot\mathrm{id}_F)=0$ for every $x\in X$.

source.place: Stacks Etale Cohomology Section 03SH after Definition 03SE, property (2) ('if Y = coprod_{i=1}^d X then the trace map is the sum map') and 'This description shows that if f has constant degree d, then the composition F -> f_*f^{-1}F -> F is multiplication by d'; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Assertion (c).* Let $\varphi=\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}\circ\operatorname{res}_{f,F}-d\cdot\mathrm{id}_F:F\to F$, a morphism in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$. Let $W\to X$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$ and $s\in F(W)$. The family $(g_x)_{x\in X}$ is etale and jointly surjective ($u_x\mapsto x$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] the projections $W_x=W\times_XU_x\to W$ form a covering of $W$ in $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Each $W_x$, with its projection to $U_x$, is an object of $(U_x)_{\Et}$ whose image in $X_{\Et}$ is $W_x\to X$; by naturality of $\varphi$, $\varphi(s)|_{W_x}=\varphi_{W_x}(s|_{W_x})$, and $\varphi_{W_x}$ is the component at $W_x$ of $g_x^{-1}\varphi$ under [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction](1), which is $0$ by step 7. So $\varphi(s)$ restricts to $0$ on every member of a covering, hence $\varphi(s)=0$ by the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Thus $\varphi=0$, i.e. $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}\circ\operatorname{res}_{f,F}=d\cdot\mathrm{id}_F$. This is (c).

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 03SH (the sentence after Definition 03SE), 04HN and Morphisms 02K9/02KB/04MH. Eight steps: (1) finite etale => finite locally free (elementary, by the definitions); (2) the fibre degree is locally constant (new node lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant, Stacks 04MH; Mathlib has Scheme.Hom.isLocallyConstant_finrank for the stalk rank, the identification with the fibre dimension is the source repository's closed finrank_eq_fiberDegree, so the node is not a leaf), hence constant d on connected X: (a); (3) the geometric fibre has Gamma of dimension d (affine computation with lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra); (4) (b) from lem-galois-geometric-fibre (Lean: Scheme.Hom.exists_overIso_sigma_of_isSepClosed, closed); (5) etale local splitting (new node lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split, Stacks 04HN) with exactly d pieces by (b) at a geometric point of the neighbourhood; (6) res and tr commute with the localization (lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction for res, property (1) of lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists for tr); (7) in the split case res is the diagonal and tr the sum (property (2)), so tr.res = d; (8) equality checked on the covering W x_X U_x of each W (lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change, sheaf condition). Statement unchanged. Property (2) of the existence lemma is used for Y' a disjoint union of d open and closed pieces each mapped isomorphically onto the base (the form 04HN gives), not for a literal coproduct; reported.
